description: CRYPTO_SPEC §5.2: the epoch-DEK commitment. dek_commitment_hex = lower_hex(SHA-256(LP("<suite>/dek-commit", project_id, environment_id, epoch, dek_hex))). The DEK and coordinates are identical to dek-wrap.json's basic vector
binary_encoding: dek_hex goes into LP as the DEK's 32 bytes in a lowercase hex string (the same convention as chain-entries.json's binary_encoding)

rewrap_invariance.note: the commitment's preimage depends on neither the wrap nor the recipient (§5.2): the commitment is invariant under a post-add_member backfill of a past epoch, a repair-path delete → re-register, changes in the same DEK's wrap ciphertext from HPKE randomness, and later widening of the recipient set. The implementation test re-wraps the same DEK afresh (HPKE Seal is randomized) and pins that the unwrapped DEK compares equal to this commitment
rewrap_invariance.wrap_reference: dek-wrap.json vectors[0] (wrap data of the same DEK)

vectors.name: basic
vectors.note: the same DEK and coordinates as dek-wrap.json's basic (epoch 3 = from a rotate)

vectors.name: epoch-1-create
vectors.note: the commitment of epoch 1 (from create_environment — §6.2). The coordinates enter the preimage, so the value differs from basic

negative.name: dek-mismatch
negative.note: a different DEK fails the commitment comparison (blocks fake-DEK injection — §5.2 / §14.2-1)

negative.name: transplant-project
negative.note: does not match a commitment of another project's coordinates (the coordinates enter the preimage)

negative.name: transplant-environment
negative.note: does not match a commitment of another environment's coordinates

negative.name: transplant-epoch
negative.note: does not match a commitment of another epoch's coordinates

negative.name: wrong-domain
negative.note: a different suite means a different domain string, so a cross-suite commitment transplant fails the comparison

negative.name: uppercase-hex
negative.note: an uppercase-hex dek_hex becomes a different byte string and fails the comparison (the canonical preimage form is lowercase hex — implementations must normalize input to lowercase hex before computing)
